replace-the-in-cell-selection-ring-inset.text: Replace the in-cell selection ring / inset shadow (#selection-ring) with a zoom-aware overlay drawn OUTSIDE the cell interior so a selected cell's full color stays visible and comfortably targetable at paint zoom. The overlay must share the same camera transform used for rendering and pointer hit testing, sit above the board without capturing paint gestures, and keep keyboard navigation and touch drag/pinch from ever submitting paint. Keep the selected color swatch visible next to the board. Acceptance: at paint zoom a chosen cell shows its entire color with the indicator fully outside the cell; adjacent painted cells still touch with no unintended gaps; corners/center still map correctly after zoom/pan/resize; touch drag and pinch do not paint; arrow-key navigation remains usable and moves the external indicator with the selection.

make-painted-cells-render-as-exact-seam-.text: Make painted cells render as exact, seam-free squares at every zoom level and device pixel ratio so a chosen cell reads as one fully colored square. Board review acceptance: 'adjacent painted cells touch without unintended gaps'. The canvas renderer `web/src/render-board.ts` currently fills rectangles (`fillRect(x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, CELL)`, CELL = 4) into a container-scaled canvas, so cell edges can leave background seams or shaved/blurred boundaries once the board is scaled into the zoomed viewport or shown on fractional-DPR displays. Correct the renderer so that: (a) neighbouring painted cells share an edge with no background-colored seam and no overlapping or anti-aliased boundary at overview zoom, painting zoom, and fit-to-wall; (b) cell edges land on device pixels (crisp) at DPR 1, 2 and fractional scaling, including when the zoom transform is fractional; (c) rendering stays a pure function of board state plus camera so it is unit-testable without DOM layout. Keep the logical 128x128 board, the eight-color palette indices, the on-chain pixel format, the existing `get_pixels` page size, and the camera/hit-test/wall-page modules untouched - keep the fix confined to the renderer module and its test. If a camera-side rounding change turns out to be genuinely required, stop and report it in the task result rather than editing the wall page or camera module. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm ci` before any verification. Add or extend unit tests in `web/src/render-board.test.ts` covering the seam/gap invariant: adjacent filled cells produce contiguous coverage with no uncovered background row/column, painted coverage equals cell area times painted cell count, and scaled cell rectangles are pixel-aligned across a zoom x DPR matrix (overview, painting zoom, fit-to-wall; DPR 1 and 2).

complete-the-board-viewport-and-toolbar-.text: Complete the board viewport and toolbar for the core painting moment on a phone. At a 390px-wide viewport the palette and the Place action must sit within reach of the board - visible without a long scroll and not pushed below the fold - with a compact connection/freshness indicator next to the board. Move contract/schema/rules/state/debug text out of the primary presentation into an expandable About/details panel so the wall is the primary surface. Label any local sample art used for visual testing as demo data. Draw the selection indicator outside the chosen cell (offset ring/overlay) so the whole cell interior stays colored. Keep pointer hit testing aligned with the rendered grid after zoom, pan and resize (all four corners and the center map correctly), and make touch drag/pinch pan or zoom without ever submitting paint; keyboard cell navigation must keep working. Reuse the existing camera transform, hit test and pending-paint layer; do not change the contract, the shared constants/palette, the draw submit path, or the placement-outcome status model. Do not add function-call key creation, change sign-in, or touch wallet/deployment code - connection state is only displayed. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm ci` before any verification. Add or extend tests under `web/src/pages/wall/` for selection-indicator geometry (indicator sits outside the cell, cell interior not obscured) and for tap-vs-drag discrimination (a drag or pinch produces zero draw submissions while a tap on a cell selects/places as before).

at-paint-zoom-a-cell-must-read-as-a-full.text: At paint zoom a cell must read as a full, crisp square of roughly 16–24 CSS px on desktop and on a 390 px viewport; adjacent painted cells must share edges with no seam, hairline, or blur; the selection indicator must be drawn outside the chosen cell's bounds so the cell's own color fills its interior at full size. Implement this in the viewport/display layer — size the canvas backing store from the active camera zoom and devicePixelRatio and keep one shared transform used by rendering, hit testing, and overlays — rather than relying on the bitmap cell constant that CSS scaling negates. Keep the 128x128 logical board. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm ci` from a clean tree before running tests or the build. Constraints: do not change the contract, `shared/**`, the palette or overwrite rules, or wallet/signing/connection modules; confine edits to the renderer, selection/overlay, camera-transform modules and their tests.

make-painting-at-zoom-precise-and-seam-f.text: Make painting at zoom precise and seam-free without touching the presentation CSS or the contract. Deliverables: (1) at paint zoom each cell renders as a complete edge-to-edge rectangle so adjacent painted cells share a boundary with no visible seam, background line, or partially filled interior at zoom levels 1x/2x/4x/8x and device pixel ratios 1/2/3; (2) a click/tap at paint zoom selects and places on the cell actually under the pointer, not a neighbour, at every zoom level, pan offset and window resize; (3) pan, pinch and drag gestures never submit a paint — only a tap that resolves to a cell may select/place, and a drag that ends on a different cell than it started must not paint. Approach: keep the 128x128 logical board, the existing fillRect(x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, CELL) geometry and the existing camera transform; do NOT change the bitmap CELL constant and do NOT edit web/src/style.css. Instead own canvas sizing in web/src/main.ts so the canvas backing store equals the displayed CSS size multiplied by devicePixelRatio (the bitmap is never upscaled by CSS), and derive pointer hit-testing, cell rects and any selection geometry from one shared device-pixel-snapped rect computation in web/src/render-board.ts. Add unit tests in web/src/render-board.test.ts for the rect math and hit-testing across those zoom/DPR combinations, including a corner cell, the centre cell, a resize case, and a drag-ends-on-another-cell case that must not submit a paint. Do not change board dimensions, palette, contract metadata handling, submit/queue logic or wallet calls. Environment: run `cd web && npm ci` first; verification runs from the repository root.

on-a-390-px-wide-viewport-reference-390x.text: On a 390 px-wide viewport (reference 390x844) the palette and the Place/confirm action sit in a bottom control bar within thumb reach and never overlap the board's paint target area; the board keeps the largest remaining height above the bar and safe-area insets are respected. The selected-cell indicator is drawn outside the chosen cell so the cell's interior stays fully colored at every zoom level (no border or inset shadow over the cell). Contract/schema/debug text stays out of the primary view and connection/freshness status stays compact. Approach: implement as HTML structure plus CSS layout only, in web/index.html and web/src/style.css (sticky/safe-area bottom bar, flex sizing so the board fills the space above it, selection indicator positioned outside the cell rect). Do NOT change submit/queue logic, wallet calls, contract reads, the draw path, or the wall page module's lifecycle or its tests — the previous attempt edited a wall-mount dispose test and was blocked; this attempt leaves that module and its tests untouched. Label any placeholder/demo art used for visual checking as demo data. Environment: run `cd web && npm ci` first; verification runs from the repository root.

deliver-device-pixel-accurate-board-rend.text: Deliver device-pixel-accurate board rendering so the paint moment is crisp and precisely targetable. The wall canvas backing store must equal its CSS size x devicePixelRatio and be refreshed on window resize and DPR change; confirmed cells must be drawn as integer-aligned rectangles covering the whole logical cell so adjacent painted cells touch with no seam, blur, or partially colored edge. This must hold at fit-to-wall zoom, at paint zoom (~16-24 screen px per cell), at DPR 1/2/3, and after pan/resize, with all four corners and the centre mapping correctly. Keep the merged zoom/pan camera transform as the single board->screen mapping and keep render-board.ts's existing public API plus the draw submission path unchanged. Add unit tests for the logical->device pixel mapping and for the full-cell-coverage invariant. No contract, palette, wallet, or deployment edits.

deliver-an-external-zoom-aware-selection.text: Deliver an external, zoom-aware selection indicator and hover preview so the chosen cell's color is never hidden. The selection indicator must be drawn outside the chosen cell's interior (offset and scaled with the camera transform) rather than as an inward border/inset shadow over it, and must remain legible and correctly positioned at fit-to-wall zoom, at paint zoom, and on the 390 px mobile layout. Hovering or selecting a cell must preview the currently selected palette color in a separate preview layer that is visually distinct from confirmed art and from pending paint, never covering a confirmed cell's color. Add unit tests asserting the indicator geometry has zero overlap with the chosen cell's interior and that the preview layer is not part of the confirmed-pixel layer. Preserve the merged zoom/pan camera transform contract and the toolbar layout from head commit 245f9c7; no contract, palette, wallet, or deployment edits.

make-the-chosen-cell-crisp-and-precisely.text: Make the chosen cell crisp and precisely targetable at paint zoom, with the cell's color never obscured. Size the wall canvas backing store to CSS size x devicePixelRatio so cells rasterize crisply, and ensure adjacent painted cells touch exactly (no gaps or 1px overlaps between neighbours) at any zoom level, pan offset or resize. Expose the selection indicator as a screen-space rect computed from the shared camera transform so it is drawn outside the chosen cell's interior (zoom-aware ring/border) and never covers the stored color; style it in the stylesheet used today. Cover both with unit tests: indicator rect lies outside the cell rect at overview zoom, paint zoom and DPR 1/2/3, and neighbour cell rects are edge-adjacent with zero gap at those zooms.

make-painting-on-a-phone-safe-and-honest.text: Make painting on a phone safe and honest: distinguish tap from drag with pointer events so panning, pinching and any two-pointer gesture never submit a draw - only an explicit Place action (or an explicitly enabled direct-paint mode) submits, and keyboard selection/placement keeps working unchanged. Render pending paint in a separate client layer that is visibly different from confirmed art (e.g. distinct badge/outline/dimmed treatment) and is cleared or reconciled by the existing submitted/confirmed/confirmation-delayed/failed/overwritten outcome states rather than being silently merged into confirmed cells. Add tests that a drag sequence, a pinch sequence and a wheel/pan gesture on the wall surface produce zero submitted draws, that a single tap plus Place produces exactly one, and that pending cells are marked as pending and never counted as confirmed.

guarantee-that-pan-pinch-and-drag-never-.text: Guarantee that pan, pinch and drag never submit paint and that queued paint is visibly distinct from confirmed art. (a) Extract gesture classification into a standalone pure module web/src/gesture.ts that converts pointer events into tap vs drag vs pan vs pinch using a movement/time threshold and pointer-count, with its own unit tests in web/src/gesture.test.ts. (b) Wire that classifier into web/src/pages/wall/mount-wall.ts with a minimal diff so only a deliberate tap (or the explicit Place action) enqueues a draw, and any gesture that moved beyond the threshold, used multiple pointers or began on the pan surface is discarded without a submit. (c) Render queued/pending cells in a separate client-side layer above confirmed pixels, derived from the existing paint queue and the existing submitted/confirmed/confirmation-delayed/failed/overwritten outcome states, with styling in web/src/style.css that is clearly different from confirmed art. (d) An uncertain request must never be auto-resubmitted when refresh or reconnect replaces board state. Do NOT modify AGENT.md, fix_plan.md or any repo-root document; no contract, wallet or economy files. Verify with web unit tests and the production build.

make-the-paint-moment-legible-and-precis.text: Make the paint moment legible and precise: render the selection indicator entirely outside the target cell (a viewport-driven overlay ring computed from the shared camera transform, never a border, outline or inset shadow drawn over the cell interior) so a painted cell always shows its full color; render cells crisply at paint zoom (integer/nearest-neighbour scaling, no blur or half-pixel seams) so two adjacent painted cells touch with no unintended gap; verify all four corners and the centre map to the correct logical cell after zoom, pan and resize. Keep every edit under web/src; do not create or modify any repo-root file (no AGENT.md, no fix_plan.md).

re-plan-of-last-batch-s-scope-violation-.text: Re-plan of last batch's scope_violation-blocked selected-cell-legibility task using a different approach: confine every change to web/src (do NOT edit AGENT.md, fix_plan.md or any docs/**), and solve legibility inside the wall renderer/overlay instead of via root documents. Draw the selection indicator entirely outside or around the target cell (or as a zoom-aware overlay anchored to the existing camera transform) so a selected cell's interior keeps the full chosen color and a just-painted cell reads as one complete square with no partial fill. Ensure adjacent painted cells touch with no unintended 1px gaps at overview, paint zoom (~16-24 screen px per cell) and maximum zoom. Reuse one shared camera transform for rendering, hit-testing, coordinates and the indicator so they cannot desync, and keep keyboard navigation and corner/center hit-testing correct after zoom/pan/resize.

make-the-wall-the-primary-element-of-the.text: Make the wall the primary element of the wall page: move the contract metadata, schema, evidence, rules and verbose connection/state text out of the main canvas view into a collapsed, expandable About/details panel; keep the palette and the Place action within reach of the board on desktop and at 390px mobile width; keep a compact testnet/connection/freshness status visible near the board. Display-only restructuring — do not change any contract, wallet, economy, pricing or deployment behavior, and edit under web/ only (no repo-root document).

re-plan-the-blocked-wall-primary-present.text: Re-plan the blocked wall-primary-presentation task with a different approach. Make the 3D stall / board the dominant visual element per the visual concept: the canvas (with the already-merged zoom-aware selection ring) is the hero of the viewport, and the large contract/schema/rules/state text currently above and beside the canvas is moved into a collapsed, expandable About/details panel (native <details>/<summary>) that sits below or beside the board and is collapsed by default. Keep the palette and the Place action within comfortable reach on a 390px mobile viewport (palette + Place grouped directly under the board, not pushed off-screen). Retain a compact testnet indicator and keep the Open-wall rule text discoverable inside the About panel rather than as a headline. Label any bundled local/sample artwork as demo data. DIFFERENT APPROACH FROM THE BLOCKED ATTEMPT: do NOT create any new CSS file (the blocked attempt added web/src/wall-design.css) and do NOT edit web/AGENT.md; express the new layout using the existing web/index.html markup, the existing wall-template CSS class structure, and additions to web/src/style.css only, so every changed path is inside the declared touches. State environment-preparation steps in the brief so verification cannot fail for environmental reasons: run `cd web && npm install` before tests.

on-the-stall-page-make-the-board-the-dom.text: On the stall page make the board the dominant primary element: the board occupies the main viewport area, the palette and the Place/tap-to-place control sit within thumb reach next to the board at 390px mobile width as well as on desktop, and contract/schema/palette/rules/debug text moves out of the main view into an expandable 'About / details' panel, while retaining a compact testnet + fee indication. Do not change board logic, viewport logic or rendering behaviour, and do not add a separate stylesheet outside web/src. The paint moment and the merged selection-ring/flush-cell work (fbf01d6) must be preserved.

make-the-live-wall-the-dominant-element-.text: Make the live wall the dominant element on desktop and at 390px mobile width, keeping the color palette and the Place action within reach of the board (adjacent/sticky, no scrolling between board and Place) as required by the board-review step-2 composition. Move contract/schema/rules version/debug/state detail out of the primary view into a collapsed, keyboard-accessible 'About / details' disclosure that is closed by default on first load, while keeping a compact testnet + fee indication visible. Limit ALL edits to web/index.html and web/src/**; do NOT modify web/AGENT.md, shared/**, contracts/**, or docs. Add/extend a unit test in web/src asserting the About panel exists and is collapsed by default and that the palette and Place controls are present in the primary view.

make-the-wall-the-dominant-element-of-th.text: Make the wall the dominant element of the page and move implementation detail out of the main view: wrap the contract id, schema version, bootstrap/rules text and raw board state into an expandable About/details panel reachable from the wall, leaving a compact testnet + connection status visible and the palette and Place action within reach on mobile. Re-plan of the blocked wall-primary-presentation task with a different, narrower approach: restructure the existing wall template markup and style.css only — add no new stylesheet or module file, do not edit web/AGENT.md or any README, and preserve every element id/class that mount-wall.ts queries so mount-wall.ts needs no change. Extend the existing wall-template test to assert the canvas/board container precedes the About panel in document order and that the contract/schema/rules text is nested inside the collapsed panel. Keep the existing responsive behaviour at 390px so palette and Place stay reachable without scrolling past debug text.

rework-the-wall-page-presentation-only-s.text: Rework the wall page presentation only, so that on desktop and at 390px mobile the board is the visually dominant element, with the palette and the Place action staying within reach of the board (never requiring scrolling away from it), while all contract/schema/overwrite-rule/state/diagnostic text collapses into a single expandable About/details panel that is closed by default (conspicuously available, keyboard-accessible, and keeping a compact testnet + no-fee indication visible). Do not change how draws are submitted, how the wallet works, or any contract behaviour; preserve existing keyboard navigation, existing DOM ids/test hooks, and the currently-merged zoom-aware selection overlay and pending-paint layer. HARD SCOPE: edit only the files listed in 'touches' (all under web/src); do NOT edit web/AGENT.md, web/package.json, web/index.html, docs, shared, or contracts, and do NOT add files outside those listed — the prior attempt at this goal was blocked for scope_violation.

harden-the-camera-transform-so-precise-p.text: Harden the camera transform so precise placement is guaranteed across zoom, pan and resize. Extend web/src/viewport.test.ts (and add cases where they are currently missing) to prove that: (a) the four board corners and the centre map to the correct cells after arbitrary zoom levels, (b) mapping stays correct after a container resize that changes the fit scale, (c) the pointer->cell mapping used by paint hit testing is exactly the inverse of the transform used to render, and (d) out-of-board pointer positions return no cell rather than clamping to an edge cell. Fix web/src/viewport.ts only if a genuine mapping defect is found; do not alter painting submission, gesture guards, the pending-paint layer, or presentation. Keep all changes inside the two viewport files listed.

make-the-canvas-board-render-crisply-at-.text: Make the canvas board render crisply at painting zoom with no hairline seams or blur, building on the existing camera transform from web/src/viewport.ts and the renderer in web/src/render-board.ts. Requirements: (a) derive a pure, exported helper (e.g. snapTransform / device-pixel-aligned camera transform) that rounds the camera translation to whole device pixels given devicePixelRatio, and use it in the render path so painted cells do not blur or leave 1px gaps between adjacent cells at any zoom level; (b) ensure the canvas backing store is sized to devicePixelRatio while the logical board geometry stays the current CELL-per-cell model, so a fully painted region renders as solid colour with touching cells (no seams between horizontal/vertical neighbours); (c) apply the CSS that keeps scaling pixel-crisp (image-rendering) where scaling still occurs, without changing board dimensions or palette; (d) unit-test the pure snapping helper (integer alignment for DPR 1, 2 and 3, and that translation snapping never changes which cell a point maps to as verified by the existing viewport hit-test function), and add a renderer-level test assertion that adjacent painted cells produce exactly abutting rectangles with no gap or overlap at the bitmap level. Keep the existing zoom/pan, gesture guards (drag/pinch never submit paint), selection overlay drawn outside the cell interior, and mobile toolbar behaviour unchanged. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm install` before verification.

wrap-the-existing-board-page-in-the-meta.text: Wrap the existing board page in the Meta Poo 3D stall composition described in docs/2026-10-12-visual-concept.md, docs/2026-10-12-stall-visual-references.md and the board review's 'Added visual guidance': back wall carrying the wall/canvas, an emblematic toilet beneath it as the focal mascot, and side walls / floor perspective extending toward the viewer, using CSS-only layered depth (perspective transforms, gradients, dark vivid geometric panels echoing the Sydney-reference palette) with no new runtime dependencies. Hard acceptance: the board remains the visual and interactive primary element — no scene element overlaps, clips, occludes or intercepts pointer events on the canvas; painting, panning, pinching and keyboard selection keep working exactly as today; at 390px wide the board, palette and Place action remain within reach without horizontal overflow, and scene decoration degrades gracefully (side walls may compress or hide, never push the board offscreen). Keep all contract/schema/rules/detail text inside the existing collapsed About/details panel; keep a compact testnet indicator if one already exists. Render scene decoration as aria-hidden presentational markup and do not add gameplay-affecting behaviour. Add or extend tests (e.g. wall-template tests) asserting the scene wrapper renders around the board, the board element still exists with its expected accessors, and no scene layer appears above the interactive board in DOM order used by existing code. Environment prep: run `cd web && npm install` before verification so a clean checkout has dependencies.

render-the-meta-poo-stall-around-the-exi.text: Render the Meta Poo stall around the existing board without touching painting mechanics. Back wall carries the canvas, a decorative toilet sits beneath it, side walls recede toward the viewer using CSS perspective, and surrounding art follows the Sydney-reference direction (vivid geometric/pixel marks on dark grounds, weathered brick/metal textures) in web/src/pages/wall/wall-template.ts + web/src/style.css. Constraints: the board keeps its existing measured size/aspect and precision (no padding/border shifting hit-test math — the camera transform and selection overlay must still land exactly on cells); palette and the Place action stay within thumb reach at 390px; the About/details panel keeps working unchanged; all decorative art is clearly labelled demo/placeholder (e.g. aria-hidden decoration plus a 'demo art' note where sample murals are shown) and never claims chain state. Extend wall-template.test.ts to assert the stall scaffold renders (back wall / side walls / toilet container present, About panel still present, demo label present) so the structure is locked. Verification commands: cd web && npm install; cd web && npm test; cd web && npm run build. Preliminary environment step is the npm install in the first command; if a lockfile exists use `cd web && npm ci` as a substitute for that command.

stop-trusting-local-constants-for-chain-.text: Stop trusting local constants for chain-shaped UI state. When a game contract is configured, load its board metadata (schema version, width, height, palette entries, overwrite rule) with a bounded timeout, and validate it against shared/board.json / shared/board-rules before enabling the Place path. On mismatch or fetch failure, keep the wall viewable read-only and surface a plain-language, compact status (e.g. 'contract metadata incompatible — drawing disabled') in the existing status/About region rather than silently painting against the wrong assumptions. Failures must be recoverable on a manual refresh; no auto-retry loop. Add tests covering: matching metadata enables drawing; wrong schema version, wrong dimensions, wrong palette length, and wrong overwrite_rule each disable drawing with a message; a timed-out/failed metadata fetch leaves drawing disabled and does not submit anything. Reuse the existing block-pinned read path where it fits; do not change the contract, wallet, or submit-draw outcome model. Verification commands: cd web && npm install; cd web && npm test; cd web && npm run build. Preliminary environment step is the npm install in the first command; if a lockfile exists use `cd web && npm ci` as a substitute.

add-an-on-board-camera-control-cluster-t.text: Add an on-board camera control cluster to the wall page: zoom in, zoom out, fit-to-wall and reset buttons, minimum 44x44px touch targets, reachable with one thumb at a 390px-wide viewport, each wired to the existing camera state and never submitting paint. Add a live coordinate readout that shows the hovered cell on desktop and the selected cell on touch as plain 'x, y' text in a fixed-width element so it never causes layout shift. Controls must stay keyboard-reachable and use the existing pan/pinch guards so pressing them cannot trigger a placement.

finish-the-instant-and-precise-paint-mom.text: Finish the 'instant and precise' paint moment in the existing camera/transform code (find it by grepping for the transform state introduced by the zoom/pan camera work under web/src). Do three narrow, reversible things: (1) when the camera is at or beyond painting zoom (roughly 16-24 screen px per logical cell), snap the transform so cell edges land on whole device pixels — no blurry half-cell scaling, adjacent painted cells must touch with no unintended gaps and no seams; below that threshold free-form overview zoom stays continuous. (2) Add a small, always-visible zoom-level readout next to the existing camera controls, with the same visual weight as the coordinate readout, and make the fit-to-wall / reset control return to a defined home view (whole wall, centred, integer scale where possible). (3) Persist camera state (zoom + pan + last home view) for the session so a resize, orientation change, or accidental reload restores the user's view instead of jumping to fit; the restore must re-clamp pan so the wall can never end up off-screen. Preserve everything that already works: touch drag and pinch must still never submit paint, tap-vs-drag distinction unchanged, keyboard navigation unchanged, external selection indicator unchanged, and no new gesture vocabulary. Do not touch layout markup, index.html, stylesheet roots, or any file outside web/src. Label nothing as shipped beyond what the code does.

add-a-compact-camera-control-group-zoom-.text: Add a compact camera control group (zoom in, zoom out, fit to wall, reset) and a live coordinate readout for the currently hovered or selected cell. Wire the controls to the existing camera transform and pointer hit testing; keep the board primary and do not restructure the surrounding page. Acceptance: at painting zoom a chosen cell is comfortably targetable; zoom/pan/resize keep the readout and controls consistent with the transform; touch drag and pinch still never place paint.

in-the-wall-page-add-a-small-camera-cont.text: In the wall page, add a small camera control cluster and live cell-coordinate readout that build on the existing zoom/pan transform. Provide four clearly labelled controls — zoom in, zoom out, fit-to-wall, reset — with min/max zoom clamping, a fit-to-wall action that preserves correct mapping after resize, and a reset that returns to the initial overview. Add a readout that shows the cell currently under the pointer or keyboard selection, plus the pending placement target when one exists; coordinates must map correctly through the existing camera transform at every zoom level and after pan. The controls and readout must be usable at 390px, touch targets should meet comfortable mobile sizing, and activating any camera control or readout interaction must never submit or queue paint. Keep the work inside the web app, reuse the landed camera/gesture/outcome layers, add focused unit tests for zoom clamping, fit/reset behavior, coordinate mapping through the camera, and no-submit camera interaction, and avoid changing shared rules or chain-facing behavior.

zoom-should-keep-the-cell-under-the-poin.text: Zoom should keep the cell under the pointer or pinch midpoint stationary instead of always zooming at the board centre. Implement this as a pure, unit-testable camera-zoom module (new file under web/src, e.g. camera-zoom.ts + camera-zoom.test.ts) that takes the current transform, a scale step, a clamp range, and an anchor point in board/screen space, and returns the new transform such that the anchor cell's screen position is invariant. Cover: zoom in and out around a cell, clamping at minimum (fit-to-wall) and maximum paint scale, fit-to-wall/reset returning to the overview with no drift, and anchor invariance for all four corners and the centre of a 128x128 board mapped through the existing camera transform. Then wire it into the existing zoom in/out and fit-to-wall controls and the pinch/tap handling already present, reusing the existing transform and hit-testing rather than introducing a second mapping. Preserve current gesture guards: a drag or pinch must still never submit paint, keyboard navigation must keep working, and touch targets must remain usable at 390px. Put new logic in new files and make only minimal wiring edits to existing modules; no index.html changes, no new root stylesheet, no edits under shared/ or contracts/.

add-a-compact-camera-control-set-and-a-l.text: Add a compact camera control set and a live cell coordinate readout to the wall. Controls: zoom in, zoom out, fit-to-wall, and reset, all driven through the existing camera transform so rendering, pointer hit testing and the selection overlay stay consistent. Coordinate readout: show the hovered cell's 'x, y' (and the selected cell's when nothing is hovered) in a small always-visible line near the palette, legible at 390px. Requirements: controls must never submit paint; zoom in/out disable at the min/max zoom limits; fit-to-wall and reset return to the overview framing; keyboard selection keeps working and updates the readout; no layout restructuring of existing sections and no new root stylesheet. Verify by rendering the page, zooming to a cell, and confirming the readout matches the cell that a tap actually paints at 390px and desktop widths.

add-a-small-mobile-first-camera-control-.text: Add a small, mobile-first camera control cluster and a live coordinate readout to the wall page, without restructuring layout or markup. Requirements: (a) four controls — zoom in, zoom out, fit-wall, reset — that drive the same camera state the existing zoom/pan transform already uses (do NOT introduce a second transform or mutate board state); (b) controls are reachable one-handed at 390px width, in the same toolbar/cluster area as the palette, with tap targets at least ~40px, and they must never submit or select a cell; (c) zoom steps are predictable (e.g. discrete factors with clamping to a min/max, fit-wall computes the factor that shows the whole board, reset returns to the fit-wall/default view and origin); (d) a coordinate readout that shows the hovered cell (desktop pointer) and the selected cell (tap/keyboard) as e.g. 'x 34, y 71', plus 'off wall' when the pointer is outside the board, and stays legible at 390px alongside the compact status line; (e) keyboard selection and arrow-key navigation keep working and update the readout; (f) DOM updates are idempotent — pan/pinch/drag and repeated renders must not thrash or steal focus from the readout. Implementation constraints: put the control/readout logic in a new module web/src/pages/wall/camera-controls.ts exporting a mount function that takes the host element and a camera-state accessor (read + set) so it stays unit-testable without a live DOM canvas; wire it from web/src/pages/wall/mount-wall.ts only (no edits to wall-template.ts, index.html, any new root stylesheet, shared/**, contracts/**, or anything under web/src owning chain reads or write submission); button/label styling goes into web/src/style.css only. Write unit tests in web/src/pages/wall/camera-controls.test.ts for clamping, fit-wall factor computation, zoom-step maths, coordinate formatting (including off-wall and out-of-range input) and reset behaviour. Environment: the only prep needed is `cd web && npm install` (already pinned by web/package-lock.json); do not add dependencies.

add-explicit-zoom-in-zoom-out-fit-to-wal.text: Add explicit zoom-in, zoom-out, fit-to-wall, and reset camera controls to the wall toolbar, plus a live coordinate readout showing the hovered or keyboard-selected cell under the pointer. The controls must adjust only the viewport and must never submit paint. Create the readout element from mount-wall.ts so wall-template.ts stays untouched in this slice.

add-a-reachable-camera-control-set-and-a.text: Add a reachable camera control set and a live coordinate readout to the wall page. Zoom-in, zoom-out, fit-to-wall and reset buttons must act on the existing camera transform already used by rendering, hit testing and overlays (no second camera state, no new pan/pinch semantics, no change to how a placement is chosen or submitted). Show a live 'cell x, y' readout for the hovered cell on desktop and the last tapped cell on touch, in the existing compact status area rather than a new panel. Buttons must be at least 44px touch targets and stay within thumb reach at 390px width, and must not intercept pointer gestures on the wall (dragging or pinching across a control must never move the camera twice or place paint). Preserve all existing selection indicators and the ability to reach every corner and the centre after zoom, pan and resize. Environment preparation: run `cd web && npm install` before verification; no other environment step is required and no new dependency may be added.

add-an-explicit-camera-control-set-to-th.text: Add an explicit camera control set to the wall's existing toolbar: zoom-in, zoom-out, fit-to-wall, and reset buttons that drive the already-landed camera transform, are comfortably tappable on a 390px viewport, and are keyboard-accessible with visible labels. Add a live coordinate readout (e.g. 'x 37 · y 91') that reflects the currently selected/hovered cell, updates as the selection moves, stays readable at 390px, and is announced to assistive tech. The controls must never submit paint; they only change the camera and the readout. Keep the existing keyboard selection working. Do not restructure the page layout, do not edit index.html, and do not introduce any new global stylesheet. Add focused unit/behaviour tests for the new controls and the readout mapping (corner and centre cells after zoom/pan).

at-paint-zoom-the-wall-must-render-as-cr.text: At paint zoom the wall must render as crisp, gap-free pixels. Disable canvas smoothing on the board surface and set nearest-neighbour image rendering on it so scaled-up cells stay sharp (no blur, no half-pixel colour bleed). Confirm painted cells abut exactly (no background hairline) at overview zoom, paint zoom and an in-between zoom, and that the zoom-aware selection indicator continues to be drawn outside the cell interior so the full cell colour stays visible. Add a regression test that pins the crisp-rendering flags and the cell-geometry invariant (cell rect derived from the same transform used for hit testing). Keep the change confined to the board rendering surface and its stylesheet: no index.html edits, no layout restructuring of the surrounding page, no camera/zoom behaviour changes.

make-the-zoomed-wall-render-crisply-and-.text: Make the zoomed wall render crisply and without seams. Today cells are drawn with fillRect and the whole board is scaled by CSS, so at painting zoom adjacent painted cells can show hairline gaps or blurry edges. Change the renderer/camera drawing path so that: (1) board pixels are drawn at device-pixel-aligned integer positions for the current camera scale, so two horizontally or vertically adjacent painted cells share exactly one boundary with no background-coloured seam; (2) the canvas uses nearest-neighbour (crisp) scaling rather than smoothed scaling when the camera magnifies, while remaining acceptable at fit-to-wall; (3) a chosen cell's interior stays a fully coloured rectangle at painting zoom (no border/inset drawn inside the cell); (4) pointer hit-testing continues to map a screen point to exactly the same cell it did before — the camera transform is the single source of truth for both drawing and hit testing, so no mapping logic is duplicated or changed in behaviour. Add unit tests covering: adjacent cells produce touching, non-overlapping rectangles; a cell's rectangle at a magnified scale covers its full footprint with integer-aligned bounds; hit-test round-trips (screen point of the centre and of each corner of a cell maps back to that cell) still hold at a magnified scale and after a pan. Keep existing tests green. Do not change board dimensions, palette handling, camera semantics (zoom limits, pan clamping), pending-paint rendering rules, or any user-facing copy. No new dependencies, no root-level stylesheet, no markup restructuring in index.html.

implement-one-reversible-web-only-slice-.text: Implement one reversible web-only slice on the existing wall page. Add a compact camera control cluster near the board: zoom in, zoom out, fit-to-wall/reset, and a visible current zoom level. Wire the controls to the existing camera transform so they never submit paint, never change the selected cell, and never synthesize a pointer tap. Clamp zoom so the minimum is fit-to-wall and the maximum keeps a cell roughly 16-24 CSS px at painting zoom; when zooming past a sensible threshold, snap or clamp cleanly rather than leaving cells sub-pixel. Show a persistent compact coordinate readout in the wall status area for the hovered cell, or the selected cell when nothing is hovered, formatted 'x, y'. Keep the controls at least 44x44 CSS px and readable at 390px; do not restructure the wall layout, introduce new dependencies, edit shared files, or change chain-facing modules. Add or extend unit tests in the existing wall test area for zoom clamping, fit/reset camera state, and pointer-to-cell mapping after fit/reset and resize. Environment preparation: from the repository root run `cd web && npm install` once before verification; the orchestrator runs verification commands from the repository root.

in-web-src-render-board-ts-make-renderin.text: In web/src/render-board.ts, make rendering device-pixel exact and seam-free for the existing board canvas. The renderer must account for window.devicePixelRatio when sizing the canvas backing store and applying the 2D context transform, so logical board coordinates map to exact device pixels. Fill each painted cell with integer-aligned rectangles (round/floor consistently) such that adjacent painted cells share an edge with no unintended CSS-scale gaps or partially colored interiors. Preserve the current visual result, palette colors, selection/pending overlay behavior, and all existing camera/zoom/pan logic. Do not modify viewport.ts, mount-wall.ts, wall-template.ts, CSS files, shared code, contracts, wallet code, or any deployment configuration. Add or extend a focused unit test file at web/src/render-board.test.ts covering devicePixelRatio 1, 2, and 3 mapping, adjacent-cell shared edges, full cell interior coverage, and unchanged color/palette output. Environment preparation: the verification commands run from the repository root and include npm install inside web/ using the existing package-lock.json; no .env, wallet, or deployed contract is required for this task.

in-the-web-renderer-module-only-make-con.text: In the web renderer module only, make confirmed cells render as exact, seam-free rectangles on the real device pixel grid so adjacent painted cells touch with no background bleeding between them at every zoom level and on both 1x and 2x/3x DPR phones. Concretely: derive each cell's rectangle from the camera transform as integer pixel edges (x0 = round(left), x1 = round(right), width = x1 - x0, likewise for y) rather than rounding the cell size, so neighbouring cells share a boundary exactly; ensure the canvas backing store used by the renderer matches its CSS pixel size multiplied by devicePixelRatio and that the renderer draws in backing-store pixels (no fractional CSS-scaled blits); disable image smoothing so zoomed cells stay crisp; keep the existing selection indicator outside the cell interior (do not fill or border any part of a confirmed cell); keep the renderer pure and free of DOM/wallet/chain imports so it stays unit-testable. Add regression tests that assert, for a grid of zoom levels and DPR 1, 2 and 3, that consecutive cell rectangles share an edge with zero gap and zero overlap and that a cell's filled rect covers its full interior. Do NOT change camera controls, viewport hit testing, templates, CSS, the pending paint layer, or anything under contracts/, shared/, or wallet code — the previous batch's camera/template/CSS attempt blocked as scope_violation, so this re-plan confines the fix to the renderer. Environment preparation: the web workspace has no installed dependencies in a fresh checkout, so run the install step below before any test/build command.

make-one-logical-board-cell-crisp-seam-f.text: Make one logical board cell crisp, seam-free and comfortably targetable when the player is zoomed in to paint. Introduce a pure metrics module (web/src/cell-metrics.ts) that converts the current camera state and the canvas's displayed size into: rendered cell pitch in CSS pixels, an integer-rounded device-pixel pitch (so neighbouring filled cells share edges with no sub-pixel gap or overlap), and the effective on-screen target size for one cell. Round cell boundaries to whole device pixels derived from window.devicePixelRatio instead of relying on CSS scaling of a fixed bitmap, and size the canvas backing store from displayed size x devicePixelRatio so a filled cell is a solid, fully coloured rectangle (cell interior never covered by the selection indicator). Wire that module into the existing render path so painting zoom yields roughly 16-24 CSS px per cell, and re-derive it on window resize and zoom change. Do NOT edit any CSS file, the toolbar layout, camera gesture handling, or any chain-facing module. Acceptance: unit tests assert that at painting zoom the cell pitch is within 16-24 CSS px, that device-pixel pitch is an integer so adjacent painted cells share an edge with zero gap or overlap, and that corners/centre still map to the same cells after a simulated resize; the production build passes. Verification is by the listed commands; include the dependency install in the same command chain so a fresh checkout cannot fail for environmental reasons.

make-board-rendering-device-pixel-exact-.text: Make board rendering device-pixel exact and seam-free at painting zoom, using only the renderer module and styling. Environment prep first: `cd web && npm install` (npm ci if a clean install is needed) so tests/build cannot fail for missing dependencies. In web/src/render-board.ts: size the canvas backing store from its CSS box multiplied by min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2) (window.devicePixelRatio-equivalent value passed in or read from the viewport, not from chain state), set the 2D context transform so one logical board pixel maps to an exact device-pixel-aligned rectangle, and draw each confirmed cell with a single fillRect whose computed left/top/width/height are integer device-pixel aligned (round/floor consistently so no 1px gap appears between neighbours). Re-apply on resize and whenever the canvas is re-rendered; keep CELL/logical dimensions from shared/board.json untouched. In web/src/style.css ensure the canvas CSS size is integral (no fractional width/height from percentage containers or device-pixel-ratio transforms that produce half-pixel cells) and that any image-rendering rule keeps cells crisp rather than blurred. Keep the pending-paint layer and selection overlay behaviour exactly as it is today; do not change camera/zoom/pan state, hit testing, toolbar layout, or any chain-facing module. Verification must show: full frontend test suite green, production build green, and the rendered board at paint zoom has no background-coloured seam between two adjacent painted cells and no partially covered cell interior.

add-a-touch-safe-hover-cursor-preview-an.text: Add a touch-safe hover/cursor preview and compact coordinate readout around the board, purely additive and never submitting paint. Environment prep first: `cd web && npm install` so tests/build cannot fail for missing dependencies. In the wall page module (web/src/pages/wall/mount-wall.ts) attach a pointermove handler on the canvas that maps the pointer position to a board cell using the EXISTING hit-test function unchanged, and passes the hovered cell to the view; clear it on pointerleave, on pointerdown-then-drag (pan), on wheel/pinch/zoom changes, and while a gesture guard is active. Render the hover highlight as an overlay OUTSIDE the cell interior (same treatment as the existing selection indicator) so the cell stays fully coloured; on coarse-pointer/touch devices do not show a hover highlight at all, and never treat hover or a completed drag/pinch as a placement. In web/src/pages/wall/wall-template.ts add a compact status line (e.g. in the board toolbar/near the wall heading) that displays the hovered or selected cell as `x, y` plus a short hint such as 'Tap a cell, then Place' when nothing is selected; keep the existing compact testnet/fee/connection status intact and keep contract/schema detail in the existing About panel. Styling goes in web/src/wall-design.css and must keep palette + Place action within reach at 390px width without overlapping the board. Do not modify camera/zoom/pan math, canvas backing-store sizing, render-board drawing, hit-test logic, or any chain-facing module. Acceptance: hovering on desktop shows a preview highlight and updates the readout without selecting or submitting; touch drag and pinch never paint and never leave a stuck hover highlight; the readout shows correct coordinates after zoom/pan/resize at corners and centre; keyboard selection still works and the readout reflects it.

make-the-painted-wall-crisp-and-seam-fre.text: Make the painted wall crisp and seam-free at painting zoom by rendering the canvas at device-pixel resolution (devicePixelRatio-aware backing store) while keeping the existing single shared camera transform for hit-testing and overlays. Acceptance: at paint zoom, adjacent painted cells touch with no hairline gaps or blurring on a 1x and a 2x DPR; the black/mock board still previews correctly; no change to the contract, wallet path, palette, or camera math used by pointers. Stay strictly inside the three declared files: web/src/render-board.ts, web/src/render-board.test.ts, web/src/style.css. Do NOT create, edit, or delete any other file — notably not fix_plan.md, remaining.json, remaining.harness.json, .ao/*, docs/**, shared/**, or contracts/**; if you believe another file must change, stop and report instead of editing it. Extend web/src/render-board.test.ts with unit coverage for the DPR-scaled canvas sizing math (e.g. that backing-store dimensions are logical size times DPR and that the reported cell rects stay in logical coordinates).

add-explicit-mobile-first-zoom-controls-.text: Add explicit, mobile-first zoom controls to the wall viewport: a compact control cluster with zoom-in, zoom-out, and fit-to-wall buttons placed within reach of the palette/Place action on a 390px viewport, wired to the existing camera transform so they behave exactly like wheel/pinch (same clamp limits, same hit-test mapping). Also bind keyboard shortcuts (plus, minus, zero for fit) alongside the existing arrow-key cell navigation, give each control an accessible label and a disabled state at the clamp limits, and make it explicit that activating a zoom control never selects, previews, or submits paint. Use the existing camera/viewport module rather than introducing a second transform; do not touch shared/, contracts/, wallet code, or any board-rule behaviour. Acceptance: after any sequence of zoom in/out/fit plus drag or pinch, all four corners and the centre of the board map to the correct cells (extend the existing corner/centre hit-test coverage); zoom controls work with touch, mouse, and keyboard; paint is never submitted by a zoom action.

make-the-wall-canvas-render-crisp-and-se.text: Make the wall canvas render crisp and seam-free at painting zoom by updating only the existing global stylesheet: opt the board canvas into pixelated image rendering, disable browser interpolation, and keep canvas presentation aligned to whole device pixels so adjacent painted cells touch cleanly without unintended gaps. Do not change TypeScript, templates, tests, contract, wallet, or economy code.

add-a-touch-safe-pointer-preview-and-com.text: Add a touch-safe pointer preview and compact cell-coordinate readout to the existing wall mount module: on pointer move/drag show the hovered cell and its x,y without ever calling draw; on pointer leave or touch cancel clear the preview; remove listeners in dispose. Use the existing wall CSS file for readout styling. Do not edit templates, tests, repo-root files, contract, wallet, or economy code; this must not submit paint.
